texto_en: Participating in the labour market means either working or looking for work. In the European Union, 2024 data show a wide difference between persons with and without disabilities, and especially low participation among people with severe disabilities.

of persons aged 20 to 64 with disabilities participated in the labour market.
Among people with severe disabilities, approximately one third participated; among those with a moderate limitation, approximately two thirds did.

This indicator measures labour-market participation, that is, being employed or actively looking for employment. A person outside the labour force is not classified in the same way as an unemployed person who is looking for work.
Distinguish labour-force participation from employment: participation means working or looking for work. They are not the same rate.
Labour-market participation and employment are different indicators.

Early leaving from education and training
In 2024, 44.2% of young people aged 18 to 24 with severe disabilities were early leavers from education or training, compared with 8.0% of young people without disabilities.

Eurostat uses the European indicator of early leaving from education and training among young people aged 18 to 24. The comparison distinguishes severe disability, any disability and no disability.
Cite the three categories —severe disability, any disability and no disability— and the age range 18–24. Do not turn the figure into school dropout for the whole population with disabilities.
The figure must remain linked to its population, territory, year and method. Separating it from that context can change its meaning.

The NEET indicator identifies young people aged 15 to 29 who are not employed and are not participating in education or training. It combines two dimensions —work and training— and therefore should not be read as a simple unemployment rate.
